paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Abaye, Shabbat 4a; [Rav] Bibi bar Abaye, Shabbat 3b; R' Yaakov bar Avi, Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 2, at the end of halakhah 3; Rav Natan bar Abaye, Chullin 95b; Rav Shimi bar Abaye, Ketubot 60a.

notes.text: The supplied אבי ביבי is malformed. The consulted Shabbat paragraph has Rav Bibi bar Abaye, supporting the bracketed [Rav]. The separate bar Avi spelling is retained rather than silently changed to bar Abaye. סה״ג means the end of halakhah 3.

The earlier Shabbat3b consultation supports bracketed Rav for supplied אבי ביבי; it is inherited evidence, not a new primary read. Wikisource provenance does not establish a printed-letter corruption or authorize a universal OCR rule. The separate Avi patronymic remains distinct from Abaye. Full Rav titles for Acha, Natan and Shimi are supplied; the exact uninspected Yaakov title remains R'. סה״ג means end of halakhah3. The list is not a newly inferred set of sons of one resolved Abaye identity.

Printed Hyman (vol. I, p. 74) reads Rav Bibi, as does Shabbat 3b. For the Jerusalem Talmud notice it reads Yaakov bar Avi, while the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:3 version names Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye. The patronymics are preserved where they occur, with no inference that all entries in the list share one father.
